item.content:encoded:
Yeah, there's your problem. x3

That said, twenty years old and more is mostly what I was talking about - see, while fantasy was shunned as a decadent genre that glorifies and romanticizes the past, sci-fi and futurism in general was welcome by the authorities and because by removing the need for your writing to happen in the present removed most of potential political objections to the content, the writers had a fairly free hand and a lot of great quality literature came from it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There is certainly a sub-set of western authors who do nothing but rehash Mary Shelley with the "scary" new tech du jour. John Crichton springs to mind. But I don't like them either.
My benchmark sci-fi authors are Heinlein, Asimov, and Clarke. Of those currently writing, David Brin is by far and away my favorite.

I should clarify that by "Russian literature" I was specifically refering to what a stuck-up professor might categorize as literature. That is; dense, obtusely symbolic, preferabbly sold by the pound, and inaccesible to the common reader without the aid of an academic. Nothing less than twenty years old, and certainly nothing from a popular genre like science fiction or fantasy, would qualify.

item.content:encoded:
I hate without reservation Russian literature, British gothic romances, Canadian pop singers, and American romantic comedy movies; so I see nothing unreasonable about disliking an entire country/genre pairing as a class.

I also tend to dislike (but with notable exceptions that keep it from being categorical) female stand-up comedians (Maria Bamford), celebrity personality cooking shows (Alton Brown), "reality" game shows (Face Off was interesting, occasionally), and political demonstrators (hard to deny the impact of Tiananmen square tank-guy). Which is closer to what I think people mean when they say they "hate anime"; not a true blanket statement specifically refering to every animation generated by Japan ever, but rather that the defining elements do not appeal to their tastes.
